claims.claim: Eusebius of Emesa was a Christian bishop of Emesa in Syria who was born around 300 in Edessa and died around 360.
He was a pupil of Eusebius of Caesarea and received his early education in Edessa before studying in Antioch and Alexandria.
Eusebius was associated with the semi‑Arian theological party, which held that Christ was similar to the Father but not of the same substance.
His exegetical method follows the Antiochene tradition, favoring literal and historical interpretation of Scripture.
A short biography of Eusebius was written by his friend George of Laodicea, indicating his prominence in the fourth‑century church.
